about: The short state of the project. Read it first; DESIGN.md has the detail and the evidence. Update it when a milestone, a decision or a dead end lands.

people.friend: plays Guitar on Expert; Windows 11 with Smart App Control on, RTX 4070 (12 GB), 16-32 GB of RAM; wants Expert only unless asked, and solo trackers on solos

goal1.what: the test song (Car Seat Headrest, Beast Monster Thing (Love Isn't Love Enough)) charted for the friend
goal1.status: delivered: v1 (guitar, bass, drums, all levels), then v1.1 (Expert only, guitar solos on Solo 1 and Solo 2)
goal1.feedback: v1 'played pretty well'. A sparse stretch around 2:28-2:35 of the original recording: the friend said to disregard it. A beat-rate re-strum of that stretch was offered as a test version; no answer yet.

milestones.open: the Windows spike on the friend's PC

milestones.done: bass and drums of the test song (in v1)
evidence before gates: tool comparison, engine evaluations on six human-charted references

songcharter chart runs end to end in the dev container on the test song and Take Me Out; Take Me Out Expert F1@50 guitar 0.909, bass 0.912, drums 0.944. Defaults since 2026-11-03: Expert only, 4 guitar takes on CUDA and 1 on the CPU, solos on allin1's solo sections, a preview after each build, sustains clipped inside the end of the audio, the work folder in the per-user cache pruned to 5 GB.
open: beat F1 0.962 on Take Me Out, 0.008 short of the rule (autochart 0.990 minus 0.02)
drum lanes: exact-lane agreement 0.285 against STRUM's 0.667
no run on a GPU yet

milestones.status: planned for WSL2; work orders in docs/work-orders/
milestones.what: a release the friend can use on his Windows PC, running in WSL2: a guided WSL setup, a one-line install, a Start-menu shortcut, a local UI, tested on his PC
milestones.plan: docs/work-orders/M4-00-plan.md: v0.1 is a guide to set up WSL, install.sh fetched from the pre-release and checked by hash (uv lanes cu132/cu126/cpu, allin1's own Python, Node, autochart with its models and its CUDA 13 provider, doctor.json, a .wslconfig with Windows' RAM minus 4 GB, a Start-menu shortcut), device checks with the CPU fallback shown, the local UI in WSL opened in the Windows browser (drop, options, progress with cancel, the static preview, zip and install into the Windows Songs folder), diagnostics, and CI end to end in ubuntu:26.04. Native Windows and the rest are M4-99; the native plan is commit f9f9377 and M4-00's appendix.
risks: peak RAM with CUDA inside 12 GB of WSL memory (a 16 GB PC) is unmeasured: on the CPU the tree peaked at 10.1 GB, allin1's runner 7.8 GB; M4-08 measures it with memory=12GB, swap 8 GB absorbs short peaks, and under 11 GB of WSL memory allin1 is left out (librosa sections)

autochart's CUDA provider in WSL needs CUDA 13 libraries (cublas 13, cudart 13, nvrtc 13, cufft 12, curand 10, cuDNN 9): the cu132 lane's wheels plus nvidia-curand hold them, and in the dev container the provider loaded past all of them (only the driver's libcuda.so.1 was missing); never run on a GPU (eval/gpu.sh's earlier runs used CUDA 12 libraries), so M4-00b (packaging/spike/cuda13-provider.sh, the owner's 5070, about 20 min) must pass before wave 1 ends; a driver under 580 leaves the guitar on the CPU

the Start-menu shortcut under Smart App Control: a .lnk written from WSL has no Mark of the Web and targets the signed wsl.exe, so it should run; untested until M4-08 (fallback: open Ubuntu, type songcharter)
the Windows browser reaches the server through WSL's localhost forwarding (default on); the server checks it from Windows with curl.exe and falls back to WSL's own address
decisions: route: WSL2, not native Windows (the owner, 2026-11-03): the friend's PC has Smart App Control on, which blocks unsigned DLLs and Python modules with no per-app exception; Linux programs in WSL2 are outside it, and onnxruntime-node's Linux build gives the guitar CUDA again
delivery: a GitHub pre-release on neb882/song-charting (the owner)
licence: MIT for songcharter's own code, LICENSE on main (the owner); NOTICE lists the third parties
uninstall: the guide offers wsl --unregister Ubuntu as the complete uninstall, with a warning to use it only if that Ubuntu holds nothing else (the owner, 2026-11-03)

golden.status: done 2026-11-03 (branch golden), with the review's four fixes: --rerun on both runs (diff fails otherwise, and on an engine whose kept output is another commit's), the output folder cleared before any check, an engine run unasked stops the run (exit 2), exit 2/3 for bad input/bugs
golden.what: python -m eval.golden run builds the seven reference songs with songcharter chart (every level, 1 take, CPU) and records per part and difficulty the onsets, scan-chart's track hash and score.py's F1; diff OLD NEW --expect PARTS flags every other change UNEXPECTED (exit 1). DESIGN 3.6, eval/README.md; the commands are in CLAUDE.md's release gate and in sc-inspector.
golden.baseline: main at 11615e2: <scratchpad>/golden/base/summary.json, all 7 songs gate OK; the kept work folders in <scratchpad>/golden/work. Environment in the dev container: EVAL_DATA=<scratchpad>/eval SONGCHARTER_GOLDEN=<scratchpad>/golden, plus SONGCHARTER_SCAN_CHART, SONGCHARTER_AUTOCHART=<scratchpad>/eval/tools/autochart and SONGCHARTER_ALLIN1_PYTHON=<scratchpad>/research/timing/venv2/bin/python. <scratchpad> is /tmp/claude-0/-home-user/5307d417-c453-5e74-8f13-b43b2df06ab1/scratchpad.
golden.cost: cold (a kept folder made, stems hard-linked): 474-1081 s a song, 80 min for the set, the guitar take most of it; warm: 44-76 s a song, 6.5 min for the set (CPU, 2 threads)

next: Use the golden charts for every change that can move a chart (the inspector runs them; the release gate needs them).

M4: the owner runs M4-00b (packaging/spike/cuda13-provider.sh in the existing WSL on the 5070, about 20 min) while wave 1 builds (M4-01, M4-02, M4-05a); it must pass before wave 1 ends. Then M4-03 and M4-04; M4-05 and M4-06; M4-07; the full review workflow; M4-08: the owner's 5070 in a fresh Ubuntu-26.04 distro with the friend's 16 GB .wslconfig written by the install, then the friend's PC (also M1a's Windows spike).
Owner: run M4-00b and send cuda13-result.json; answer M4-00's question (Smart App Control on for the test, only if its switch is not greyed out).
Before the next quality decision: grow the reference set to 20 or more human charts, with human-charted solos among them.

dead_ends.what: filling sparse guitar stretches from pick-noise strumming
dead_ends.why: held-out precision 0.22 (6/27); an audio-free baseline did as well (10/39); 16th-note detection 0/22. No fill built.

dead_ends.what: solos by the stems rule (vocals quiet, guitar loud)
dead_ends.why: it rejects the real Car Seat Headrest solos (vocal stem active 0.56-0.95 of their frames); the default is now allin1's solo label
+0.006 over 1 with the default start and riskier; 4 beat 3 by +0.022. Use 4 on a GPU, 1 on a CPU.

dead_ends.what: autochart's transcriber on WebGPU under WSL
dead_ends.why: the adapter is lavapipe, software Vulkan on the CPU (1031 s against 319 s on CUDA); the transcriber is pinned to the requested device
the stems came out 1105 samples (the encoder delay) late; separate the decoded array

deferred: The preview's overview does not draw the solo spans.
A 1 s, 4 s or silent song exits 3 (a bug) when the librosa sections fallback raises its ParameterError; it should be a clean exit 2, perhaps with a minimum song length.
autochart's engine reports no memory peak of its own.
Q26: the build's grid period does not reach the ADTOF engine as beat_s.
Pruning: a run whose work folder is moved to the trash between its mkdir and its first marker write (a window of microseconds) fails with exit 2.
Not run on Windows: the \\?\ deletion, a rename refused while a file is open (emulated), Node's long paths.

Golden charts: a change to the separation's code does not show (every run reads the kept stems; delete the kept folders to make them again); sections, song.ini and the audio are not compared; one CPU take, so the CUDA default of 4 spliced takes is not covered.
